title: True Pixel-wise Full-frame Standard-based Analysis: Pitfalls and Benefits
content: In the realm of SEM (scanning electron microscopy), an energy-dispersive X-ray spectrometer (EDS) is typically the detector used for elemental qualitative and quantitative microanalysis. Modern EDS analysis commonly includes the acquisition and processing elemental maps from hyperspectral data cubes. Many SEM and EDS systems include options for “live” EDS quantitative mapping (i.e., quantitative elemental maps that can be acquired, processed, and displayed concurrently with the acquisition of an electron image). There are many reasons why EDS quantitative microanalysis via map acquisition does not have the same level of quality as EDS analysis performed in carefully controlled spot mode acquisition. In this work, we present methods for acquiring and processing low magnification (large field of view) quantitative elemental maps with analytical quality at each pixel as close to the quality achieved by conventional standard-based EDS analysis as possible.
